Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 95, verse 1–8:

Surah al-Tin is Meccan, and it has eight verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By the fig and the olive,﴾ ﴿and Mount Sinin,﴾ ﴿and this secure land,﴾ ﴿We have indeed created man in the best of stature,﴾ ﴿then We returned him to the lowest of the low,﴾ ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward uninterrupted.﴾ ﴿So what causes you to deny the Judgment after this?﴾ ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾

Al-Tin (the fig): it is the well-known fruit, and it is also the name of a mountain. The opinions of the exegetes concerning it will come.

﴿By the fig and the olive,﴾ ﴿and Mount Sinin,﴾ ﴿and this secure land,﴾ ﴿We have indeed created man in the best of stature,﴾ ﴿then We returned him to the lowest of the low,﴾ ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward uninterrupted.﴾ ﴿So what causes you to deny the Judgment after this?﴾ ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾.

This surah is Meccan according to the majority. Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah said it is Madani. When the previous surah mentioned the one whom Allah perfected in creation and character and preferred over all of creation, this surah mentions the state of the one who opposes him, and that He returns him to the lowest of the low in this world and the Hereafter. Allah, exalted is He, swore by what He swore by that He created him prepared to accept the truth, then He moved him, as He willed, to the lowest state. The apparent meaning is that al-tin and al-zaytun are the two well-known by this name. In a hadith there is praise of the fig, and that it cuts off hemorrhoids and benefits gout. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿and a tree that grows out of Mount Sinai﴾ [al-Muminun: 20]. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Nakhaʿi, ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah, Jabir ibn Zayd, Muqatil and al-Kalbi. Ka'b and Ikrimah said: Allah, exalted is He, swore by their places of growth, for the fig grows abundantly in Damascus and the olive in Iliya, so He swore by the two lands. Qatadah said: they are two mountains in al-Sham, on one of them is Damascus and on the other is Bayt al-Maqdis. End of quote. In the poetry of al-Nabigha, al-tin is mentioned and explained as an elongated mountain. Al-Nabigha said:

*Sahb al-zilal atayna al-tin ʿan ʿurud / yuzjina ghaiman qalilan ma'uhu shabima*

It was also said: they are two mosques, and they differed greatly about their locations; we turn away from that. There is no disagreement that Mount Sinai (Tur Sina') is a mountain in al-Sham, and it is the one where Allah, exalted is He, spoke to Musa, peace be upon him. The meaning of ﴿Sinin﴾ is "the one with trees." Ikrimah said: "good and blessed." The majority read ﴿Sinin﴾, while Ibn Abi Ishaq, ʿAmr ibn Maymun (p-490) and Abu Rajaʾ read it with a fatha on the sin, and this is the dialect of Bakr and Tamim. Al-Zamakhshari said: like *Sinun* and *Birun* it permits inflection with waw and ya', and keeping the ya' while moving the nun with the inflectional vowels. End of quote. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, ʿAbdullah, Talhah and al-Hasan read *Sina'* with a kasra on the sin and a long vowel; ʿUmar also, and Zayd ibn ʿAli, read it with a fatha and a long vowel. It is a Syriac word, and the dialects of the Arabs have varied in it. Al-Akhfash said: *Sinin* is a tree, its singular being *sininah*.

(﴿And this secure land﴾) is Mecca, and *amin* is an intensive form, meaning: safe are those within it and those who enter it, and what is in it of birds and animals; or from *amina al-rajulu* (with a damma on the mim) *amanatan*, so he is *amin*, and its security is that it guards whoever enters it, and nothing in it of birds or animals is harmed, just as the trustworthy person guards what is entrusted to him. It may also be in the sense of a passive participle from *amannahu*, because it is protected from calamities, just as it is described as *amin* in His saying: ﴿a sanctuary secure﴾ [al-Qasas: 57], in the sense of having security. The meaning of swearing by these things is to make clear their nobility and the good that appeared in them through the dwelling of the prophets and the righteous. The growing place of the fig and olive is the migration place of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and the birthplace and upbringing of ʿIsa. Al-Tur is the place where Musa, peace be upon him, was called. Mecca is the place of the birth and mission of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the place of the House which is ﴿a guidance for the worlds﴾.

﴿In the best of stature﴾: al-Nakhaʿi, Mujahid and Qatadah said: the goodness of his form and his senses. It was also said: the uprightness of his stature. Abu Bakr ibn Tahir said: his intellect and comprehension, which We adorned with discernment. Ikrimah said: his youth and his strength. The better view is generality in everything that is best. Here *al-insan* is a generic noun, and *ahsan* is an adjective of an omitted noun, meaning: in a stature that is best.

﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾: Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and al-Nakhaʿi said: with old age, the loss of reason, and the dominance of senility until he comes to know nothing. As for the believer, the pen is lifted from him. The exception on this view is disjunctive, and the meaning is not that every person undergoes this, but that among the species there are those who undergo it. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Abu al-ʿAliyah, Ibn Zayd and also Qatadah said: ﴿the lowest of the low﴾ means in the Fire, because of his disbelief; then the exception is connective. The majority read *safilin* indefinite, while ʿAbdullah read *al-safilin* definite with the alif and lam. Al-Zamakhshari took the sayings of the early scholars and beautified them with his eloquence and the choice of his words, and said: "in the best proportion for his shape and form and the balancing of his limbs; then the outcome of his affair was when he did not thank the blessing of that beautiful, upright, balanced creation, so We returned him to the lowest of those who are lowest in creation and composition, meaning the most ugly of those who are ugly in form and the most deformed in creation, and they are the people of the Fire, and the lowest of those who are lowest among the people of the levels; or: then We returned him after that shaping and beautifying to the lowest of those who are lowest in beauty of form and appearance, when We reversed him in his creation, so that his back bent after being straight, his hair turned white after being black, his skin wrinkled after being smooth, his hearing and sight dimmed after being sharp, and everything in him changed: his walk became shuffling, his voice faint, his strength weak, and his dignity senile." End of quote. In it there is exaggeration. On the view that this return is to old age, the meaning is: but the righteous among the aged have a reward that is lasting and uninterrupted, for their obedience and their patience under Allah's trial with decrepitude and old age. In a hadith: "If he reaches one hundred and has not acted, there is written for him the like of what he used to do in his health, and no sin is written against him." And also in it: "Indeed the believer, when he is returned to the most abject age, there is written for him what he used to do in his strength." That is ﴿a reward not interrupted﴾, *mamnun* meaning cut off, that is, counted and bestowed upon them as a favour.

The address in ﴿So what causes you to deny﴾ is to the disbelieving human being, as the majority said, meaning: what is it that makes you deny the Judgment, that makes you set up rivals to Allah and claim there is no resurrection after these proofs? Qatadah, al-Akhfash and al-Farra' said: Allah said to His Messenger ﷺ: then what is it that denies you in what you report of recompense and resurrection, which is the Judgment, after these lessons whose consideration necessitates the truth of what you have said?

﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ is a warning to the disbelievers and an announcement of His justice, exalted is He.

Al-Zamakhshari took the sayings of the early scholars and beautified them with his eloquence and the choice of his words, and said: "in the best proportion for his shape and form and the balancing of his limbs; then the outcome of his affair was when he did not thank the blessing of that beautiful, upright, balanced creation, so We returned him to the lowest of those who are lowest in creation and composition, meaning the most ugly of those who are ugly in form and the most deformed in creation, and they are the people of the Fire, and the lowest of those who are lowest among the people of the levels; or: then We returned him after that shaping and beautifying to the lowest of those who are lowest in beauty of form and appearance, when We reversed him in his creation, so that his back bent after being straight, his hair turned white after being black, his skin wrinkled after being smooth, his hearing and sight dimmed after being sharp, and everything in him changed: his walk became shuffling, his voice faint, his strength weak, and his dignity senile." End of quote. In it there is exaggeration. On the view that this return is to old age, the meaning is: but the righteous among the aged have a reward that is lasting and uninterrupted, for their obedience and their patience under Allah's trial with decrepitude and old age. In a hadith: "If he reaches one hundred and has not acted, there is written for him the like of what he used to do in his health, and no sin is written against him." And also in it: "Indeed the believer, when he is returned to the most abject age, there is written for him what he used to do in his strength." That is ﴿a reward not interrupted﴾, *mamnun* meaning cut off, that is, counted and bestowed upon them as a favour.

The address in ﴿So what causes you to deny﴾ is to the disbelieving human being, as the majority said, meaning: what is it that makes you deny the Judgment, that makes you set up rivals to Allah and claim there is no resurrection after these proofs? Qatadah, al-Akhfash and al-Farra' said: Allah said to His Messenger ﷺ: then what is it that denies you in what you report of recompense and resurrection, which is the Judgment, after these lessons whose consideration necessitates the truth of what you have said?

﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ is a warning to the disbelievers and an announcement of His justice, exalted is He.

Commentary of Abu Hayyan (al-Bahr al-Muhit) on surah 95, verse 1–8:

Surah al-Tin is Meccan, and it has eight verses.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By the fig and the olive,﴾ ﴿and Mount Sinin,﴾ ﴿and this secure land,﴾ ﴿We have indeed created man in the best of stature,﴾ ﴿then We returned him to the lowest of the low,﴾ ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward uninterrupted.﴾ ﴿So what causes you to deny the Judgment after this?﴾ ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾

Al-Tin (the fig): it is the well-known fruit, and it is also the name of a mountain. The opinions of the exegetes concerning it will come.

﴿By the fig and the olive,﴾ ﴿and Mount Sinin,﴾ ﴿and this secure land,﴾ ﴿We have indeed created man in the best of stature,﴾ ﴿then We returned him to the lowest of the low,﴾ ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward uninterrupted.﴾ ﴿So what causes you to deny the Judgment after this?﴾ ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾.

This surah is Meccan according to the majority. Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah said it is Madani. When the previous surah mentioned the one whom Allah perfected in creation and character and preferred over all of creation, this surah mentions the state of the one who opposes him, and that He returns him to the lowest of the low in this world and the Hereafter. Allah, exalted is He, swore by what He swore by that He created him prepared to accept the truth, then He moved him, as He willed, to the lowest state. The apparent meaning is that al-tin and al-zaytun are the two well-known by this name. In a hadith there is praise of the fig, and that it cuts off hemorrhoids and benefits gout. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿and a tree that grows out of Mount Sinai﴾ [al-Muminun: 20]. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Nakhaʿi, ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah, Jabir ibn Zayd, Muqatil and al-Kalbi. Ka'b and Ikrimah said: Allah, exalted is He, swore by their places of growth, for the fig grows abundantly in Damascus and the olive in Iliya, so He swore by the two lands. Qatadah said: they are two mountains in al-Sham, on one of them is Damascus and on the other is Bayt al-Maqdis. End of quote. In the poetry of al-Nabigha, al-tin is mentioned and explained as an elongated mountain. Al-Nabigha said:

*Sahb al-zilal atayna al-tin ʿan ʿurud / yuzjina ghaiman qalilan ma'uhu shabima*

It was also said: they are two mosques, and they differed greatly about their locations; we turn away from that. There is no disagreement that Mount Sinai (Tur Sina') is a mountain in al-Sham, and it is the one where Allah, exalted is He, spoke to Musa, peace be upon him. The meaning of ﴿Sinin﴾ is "the one with trees." Ikrimah said: "good and blessed." The majority read ﴿Sinin﴾, while Ibn Abi Ishaq, ʿAmr ibn Maymun (p-490) and Abu Rajaʾ read it with a fatha on the sin, and this is the dialect of Bakr and Tamim. Al-Zamakhshari said: like *Sinun* and *Birun* it permits inflection with waw and ya', and keeping the ya' while moving the nun with the inflectional vowels. End of quote. ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, ʿAbdullah, Talhah and al-Hasan read *Sina'* with a kasra on the sin and a long vowel; ʿUmar also, and Zayd ibn ʿAli, read it with a fatha and a long vowel. It is a Syriac word, and the dialects of the Arabs have varied in it. Al-Akhfash said: *Sinin* is a tree, its singular being *sininah*.

(﴿And this secure land﴾) is Mecca, and *amin* is an intensive form, meaning: safe are those within it and those who enter it, and what is in it of birds and animals; or from *amina al-rajulu* (with a damma on the mim) *amanatan*, so he is *amin*, and its security is that it guards whoever enters it, and nothing in it of birds or animals is harmed, just as the trustworthy person guards what is entrusted to him. It may also be in the sense of a passive participle from *amannahu*, because it is protected from calamities, just as it is described as *amin* in His saying: ﴿a sanctuary secure﴾ [al-Qasas: 57], in the sense of having security. The meaning of swearing by these things is to make clear their nobility and the good that appeared in them through the dwelling of the prophets and the righteous. The growing place of the fig and olive is the migration place of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and the birthplace and upbringing of ʿIsa. Al-Tur is the place where Musa, peace be upon him, was called. Mecca is the place of the birth and mission of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the place of the House which is ﴿a guidance for the worlds﴾.

﴿In the best of stature﴾: al-Nakhaʿi, Mujahid and Qatadah said: the goodness of his form and his senses. It was also said: the uprightness of his stature. Abu Bakr ibn Tahir said: his intellect and comprehension, which We adorned with discernment. Ikrimah said: his youth and his strength. The better view is generality in everything that is best. Here *al-insan* is a generic noun, and *ahsan* is an adjective of an omitted noun, meaning: in a stature that is best.

﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low﴾: Ikrimah, al-Dahhak and al-Nakhaʿi said: with old age, the loss of reason, and the dominance of senility until he comes to know nothing. As for the believer, the pen is lifted from him. The exception on this view is disjunctive, and the meaning is not that every person undergoes this, but that among the species there are those who undergo it.
